entries.name: (Location) Whisper Bridge
entries.content: The Whisper Bridge is the bridge leading from the front gate to the Kurosawa House. The bridge is separated from the village and the Kurosawa House by two large gates at either end. Before the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual, the Altar Twins are lead across the bridge by Veiled Priests.

entries.name: (Ghost) Veiled Priests
entries.content:
Veiled Priests, known in Japanese as Kao o kakushita guuji (Priest with hidden face), are hostile male spirits. Revered in All God's Village as the spiritual authorities, the veiled priests represented the four main families in the village's ceremonies and rituals. The veiled priests were charged with protecting the Twin Shrine Maidens and guarding sacred areas of the village, and they continued to uphold the village's spiritual customs even after death. They often attack Mio Amakura during her search for her sister and her investigation of the village's deepest, darkest rituals.

≪ Background ≫
The veiled priests acted as direct attendants to the head priest and ceremony master, the last of whom was Ryokan Kurosawa. They reported directly to the head priest any news of potential Kusabi sacrifices as well as the activities of the Mourners and Twin Shrine Maidens. They also helped to prepare and execute the Cutting Ritual and Hidden Ceremony during times of need. The number of veiled priests is unknown, but there were at least 30+, possibly implying that all male villagers of a certain status fill the role during rituals.

The veiled priests took part in the final Crimson Sacrifice Ritual. Due to Yae's absence the priests were forced to hang Sae and toss her body into the Hellish Abyss. Because it was improperly performed, the ritual failed and the Repentance occurred, killing all denizens of the village. The veiled priests were the first to face the Malice that poured forth from the abyss before it enveloped the entire village in darkness. The multitude of villagers, including the priests, continued in death to act out that fateful day, seeking out another sacrifice to appease the Abyss.

≪ Appearance ≫
Although there are many of them, the veiled priests all appear and sound identical. They wear the garb of Shinto priests (Kannushi) in all black, which is unusual of traditional priest wear. Their robe also has red trims and a red rope belt. Their most interesting features are their covered veiled faces and their skin.

All veiled priests wear a large, rectangular ofuda talisman as a veil. The priests wear these veils to prevent accidental glimpses into the Hellish Abyss, which causes blindness and insanity.

All veiled priests have sacred texts written all over their skin. This is likely a reference to the famous Japanese ghost story of Hoichi the Earless, (a man who covered his skin in sacred writings to prevent being detected by spirits, but neglected to cover his ears).

They carry with them metal Buddhist staves (Shakujou) that jingle to announce their presence.

≪ Battle ≫
Frequent battles with veiled priests reveal set patterns in their behavior. They attack in two main ways:

‣ Their main physical attack consists of a downward, overhead strike with their staff. This attack takes some time for them to execute, and in mid-arc they reveal a Fatal Frame chance.
‣ Their second attack consist of swinging their staff forward and summoning projectile spirits from its tip. The summoned spirits are small, but they hone in on the closest target and can cause significant damage if neglected. The projectiles can be photographed to make them disappear, however this inflicts no damage to the priest.

Although they move slowly, veiled priests frequently disappear, reappear and float around. Their staff and projectile attack also give them more range than other ghosts. They can become more dangerous when Mayu is present, as they often target and attack her directly, however, this also opens opportunities to ready stronger shots.

entries.name: (Term) Twin Shrine Maidens
entries.content:
The Twin Shrine Maidens are twins from the female gender chosen to perform the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual. In the ritual, the younger twin, considered to be the older twin by the village, must strangle the older twin, considered to be the younger twin by the village, in order to unite the two as one.

Twins around the age of 15 were eligible for the ritual, but there have been extreme cases where younger twins were used. Kureha is a rare example of the ritual being completed outside the normal procedure. Her twin being a stillborn, resulting in her being born with white hair as a remaining.

The male version is called Altar Twins.

≪ Known Twin Shrine Maidens/Altar Twins ≫
‣ Akane and Azami Kiryu
‣ Yae and Sae Kurosawa
‣ Mio and Mayu Amakura
‣ Tsuzuri and Musubi Osaka
‣ Itsuki and Mutsuki
‣ Ryokan Kurosawa and unnamed brother
‣ Kureha and stillborn twin

entries.name: (Ghost) Mourners
entries.content:
Mourners are hostile male spirits.

≪ Background ≫
Mourners are blind servants who spend the remainder of their lives in the underground tunnels. They fill both menial and ritual functions. Mourners maintain the tunnel system, assist the veiled priests, and attend the Hellish Abyss, especially when direct contact with the abyss is necessary, such as throwing sacrifices in while the priests and onlookers maintain a safer distance.

A prerequisite to receiving the role: all Mourners have gone blind and partly insane from glancing into the Hellish Abyss, either from accidental or forced exposure. It can be assumed the majority were former criminals within Minakami, since the common punishment for crime within the village is to be forced to look into the Hellish Abyss, blinding the criminal and condemning them to spending their life thereafter as a Mourner.

≪ Appearance ≫
Mourners are all male, and appear to wear a hakama skirt or similar on their lower halves, secured with a rope at the waist. They do not wear an upper garment. Instead, a thick rope is crisscrossed over their bare chests and upper backs, and wound around their arms . Mourners are bald or have their hair closely shorn to their heads, and a simple blind fold with sacred writing upon it is worn over their eyes. Mourners have the build of an emaciated manual laborer, never speak, though they emit guttural sounds, and are encountered exclusively in underground spaces, often in groups.

≪ Battle ≫
Despite being blind, the Mourners can still figure out where someone is if they start to run. After hitting one of them with a camera shot, they'll start to swing their arms around wildly. If someone happens to be in their attack range, they can hit them multiple times, inflicting a lot of damage. They also appear in groups in of at least 2 or 3 and can get tricky when surrounded by them. The best way to take them out is to lure them all to one side and take shots at them. Mio encounters 8 Mourners in the Underground Passage when on her way to the Hellish Abyss to save Mayu and have the final battle with the Kusabi.

entries.name: (Ghost) Sunken Woman
entries.content:
Sunken Woman is a hostile female spirit.

In the years before Mio Amakura and Mayu Amakura reached Minakami Village, the Sunken Woman had also wandered in by accident. While crossing Whisper Bridge, she was pulled into the river by several ghost hands, where she quickly met her end.

Her Spirit Stone reveals her final thoughts as she was being dragged underwater, and taking a picture of the hole in Whispering Bridge shows her surprised face before she was pulled under.

entries.name: (Ghost) Kusabi
entries.content:
Kusabi is a powerful hostile male spirit.

≪ Background ≫
The term "Kusabi" refers to a sacrifice to buy time until the Crimson Sacrifice can be performed to properly prevent the Repentance.

Seijiro Makabe was made into a Kusabi. Otherwise known as "The Folklorist", he was a personal colleague of Dr Kunihiko Aso. He had originally come to the village to observe and take pictures of the Crimson Sacrifice ritual, bringing the Camera Obscura with him. The villagers had other plans for him however, and decided that since the twins had yet to complete their purification rituals, he was to be used for a hidden sacrifice to satisfy the Malice and keep it from overcoming the village. While this did buy time for the villagers, it backfired when the Crimson Sacrifice ritual failed. The soul of the folklorist came back as the Kusabi with the soul of Sae as well, enveloping the village and everyone inside in the Malice.

Kusabi cannot be harmed until his final fight. He also can kill Mio in one hit.

≪ Death ≫
By studying the room where the ritual took place, one can assume that the sacrifice is first bound in rope and suspended in the air by various mechanisms as they pull the ropes tightening and eventually breaking the bones of the sacrifice. One journal that can be found states that "The more the sacrifice suffers, the more satisfied the Abyss becomes". It is also learned that the Kusabi undergoes the Cutting Ritual prior to being sacrificed into the Hellish Abyss. They are repeatedly slashed and cut all over their body.

Furthermore, the Kusabi is to be tortured only until they are on the very brink of death. If the Kusabi is to die before being thrown in the Abyss, the ritual will be a failure. The failed Kusabis, or those who died before being thrown into the Abyss, are buried in the stone walls of the Underground Passageway leading from the Rope Room in the Kurosawa House to the Hellish Abyss.

Observing the Kusabi yields sight of his right arm that appears to have been severed at some point during his torture. The arm looks to have been both nailed and tied back onto Seijiro's body, likely due to a lack of clarification regarding the rules for throwing the sacrifice's entire body into the Hellish Abyss.

≪ Battle
Upon entering the room where the ghost of Sae can be seen laughing among dead bodies, the Kusabi will appear and give chase. There is nothing that can hurt him. The camera doesn't seem to affect him and instead the pictures taken become warped and blurred. He will kill Mio instantly just by touching her, even if she has a Stone Mirror.

At the end of her journey, however, Mio will have to fight him. Kusabi is extremely strong, only able to be damaged with a Fatal Frame or Zero Shot and with powerful film.

entries.name: (Ghost) Limbo Man
entries.content: Limbo Man is a hostile male spirit. Not much is known about him in life, however he was in attendance at the Kurosawa House during the ritual when the Repentance happened. He is killed by Kusabi in the Bloodstained Room along with Limbo Woman. When entering the home, he can be seen being dragged by Kusabi along a hallway. His ghost can be seen having visibly deep wounds, a missing eye, and a lost arm.

entries.name: (Ghost) Limbo Woman
entries.content:
Limbo Woman is a hostile female ghost.

≪ Background ≫
Little is known about this ghost. She was most likely from one of the main houses since she was at the Kurosawa House at the time of the Repentance. It can be assumed that she is a victim of the Kusabi and was cut up due to her condition. She will usually appear if the Limbo Man is present.

≪ Battle ≫
She isn't so hard in battle, she may move about a bit, but as long as she isn't fought in an enclosed space she should be easy, the worst fight with her is when she fights alongside Limbo Man in a small room.

entries.name: (Location) Hellish Abyss
entries.content:
The Hellish Abyss, known in Japanese as the Utsuro (虚: Void, Hollow), is the central ritual site of All God's Village. The abyss is where the sacred Crimson Sacrifice Ritual is performed, and it is both feared and revered in village folklore.

≪ Appearance and Characteristics ≫
The Hellish Abyss appears as a perfectly square, open hole, found in the system of underground tunnels (both natural and minded) beneath Minakami Village. Whether is was discovered this way, or created is unknown. They Abyss is left uncovered.

The Abyss is in a large, underground chamber, several stories in height, with a torii gate over the entrance tunnel. This chamber is plain and empty of all other features or adornments, except a few torches and a plain, rectangular, stone altar. The altar is cushion shaped, approximately knee height, large enough for a grown person to lay on, with the head of the altar facing towards the Abyss.

The Abyss lies directly underneath the sacred altar and ring of stones on Misono Hill.

Those who look into the Hellish Abyss go insane and are immediately blinded. Speaking of the Abyss directly causes people to become mute. Taking a picture of the Hellish Abyss with the Camera Obscura reveals a teeming mass of spirits in the darkness. The Taboo Tome implies that whatever is in the Abyss can communicate with those outside of it, and listening to it will destroy a person's soul or turn them heartless.

The Abyss causes earthquakes, and expels a miasma-like malice, which corrupts those who come in contact with it, and drives them insane. In spite of being feared and viewed as an entryway to the land of the dead, the village also appears to attribute their source of life and prosperity to it, since it is used to create the Remaining, who act as local kami, blessing the village.

It is unclear if the Abyss feeds off of negative emotions, such as pain, suffering, and resentment, with a sufficient amount of these emotions appeasing it for a period, or if the Abyss becomes temporarily sealed after sacrifices because the sacrificed were ready and willing to die, with no earthly attachments (because of the aforementioned suffering).

≪ Background ≫
The Hellish Abyss is a sacred site steeped in village folklore. It has long been regarded as a gateway to the land of the dead, however, its origin has never been made clear. The abyss is also the center of the earthquakes that occur in the surrounding region. After some periods of peace, the land surrounding the abyss would quake, which the villagers would take as an omen of future disaster and misfortune. Criminals are forced to look into the Abyss and, once blinded by the sight, are turned into mourners, who live their lives in the tunnels, attending to the Abyss and to the Veiled Priests.

In order to calm the abyss and prevent the evil energy it holds within from seeping out, sacrifices are made to appease it. An ordinary human sacrifice was not enough, however, and this need gave birth to the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual.

The Crimson Sacrifice Ritual entails the sacrifice of the younger twin sibling. Identical twins are born relatively frequently in All God's Village, and they are thought to be special, holding power above that of ordinary humans. By completing the ritual, the souls of the twins are thought to become one, and the immense energy created by that process, in turn, seals the Hellish Abyss for years. The sacrificed twin becomes a Crimson Butterfly, and journeys to the other side of the abyss, while the remaining twin guards the earthly realm.

The Crimson Sacrifice Ritual occurs only after twins are born and raised to a certain age. During the time between, the Hellish Abyss would occasionally rumble, and measures must be taken to momentarily calm it. Because of this, the villagers also practiced a Hidden Ceremony, wherein an outsider to the village is taken in and made into a human sacrifice. The sacrifice, named a Kusabi, is mutilated and cut, but kept alive so that the pain would act to pacify the abyss when they are finally thrown into it. More pain suffered by the Kusabi would hold back the darkness of the abyss for longer, however, this ritual's effects were temporary, meant only to delay disaster until the proper Crimson Sacrifice Ritual is held.

Although the abyss is revered the sacred site of these rituals, it is primarily feared as a passageway into the land of the dead. The rituals described are performed to appease the abyss and prevent the darkness from escaping and corrupting the village, A catastrophe villagers referred to as The Repentance. Merely speaking of the abyss is viewed as a taboo in the village, as any exposure to the abyss is known to inflict suffering.

entries.name: (Location) Misono Hill
entries.content:
Misono Hill is a landmark in Minakami Village.

The path of this hill is the only one known to lead into Minakami Village, located south of it with a Shinto torii marking the entrance. After the village disappeared during the Repentance, anyone who became lost in the surrounding area came to the village via this hill. Once someone crosses the torii, the path behind vanishes into the dark and the person is trapped within the village.

Right in the middle of the hilltop is a stone pedestal known as the Offering Stone. This is what Masumi Makimura studied during his exploration of the village and determined it to be a sort of "cover" for a hole.

This hill also played a role in the festival relating to the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual. Torches were lit at the beginning of the ceremony, and the Offering Stone was moved away from the hole. The villagers would gather on the hill, surrounding the stone, chanting and offering up prayers for the Sacrificed Twin soul. At the same time, Veiled Priests would chant the Sacrificial Song together underground at the site of the ritual. Mayu has mentioned that, although there is no one to be seen on the hill, she thought she heard "singing", which may refer to the priests' song.

The stone lies directly above the Hellish Abyss, which would explain the hole.

entries.name: (Location) Underground Passageway
entries.content:
The Underground Passageway is a very long passage underneath the Kurosawa House which leads to the Hellish Abyss. At one point it was a network of linked passages and caves, used to get between houses, but by the time Mio and Mayu entered Minakami Village, a series of collapses had made it impassable in many places. One of the places it originally led to was the Earth Bridge, the cellar beneath the Osaka House and the path beneath the Kureha Shrine. Some of the dry wells in Minakami were connected to the caves, and the movement of the wind caused a resonant, eerie sound.

The passageway is haunted by Mourners, as they were not allowed above ground.

Veiled Priests, Twin Shrine Maidens, and Kusabi all entered the passageway via the Rope Temple of the Kurosawa House. Part of the passage was lined with the bodies of failed Kusabi, who died during the Cutting Ritual and were therefore not fit to be used as sacrifices.

entries.name: (Location) Storehouse
entries.content: The Storehouse was an area maintained by the Tsuchihara family that was used to hold the criminals of Minakami Village. Itsuki Tachibana was imprisoned there after attempting to help Sae and Yae Kurosawa escape the village and later hung himself inside there.

entries.name: (Location) Earth Bridge
entries.content: The Earth Bridge was one of two passages which connect the Kiryu and Tachibana Houses, along with the Heaven Bridge. It was used to cross from one house to the other while a twin occupied a house each, in preparation for their Crimson Sacrifice Ritual.

entries.name: (Location) Tachibana House
entries.content:
The Tachibana House was one of the houses of Minakami Village. It was connected to the Kiryu House via the Heaven Bridge and Earth Bridge. This house temporarily housed twins who were undergoing purification before participating in the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual as well as the Tachibana family itself, including twins Itsuki and Mutsuki and their little sister Chitose.

entries.content:
The Rope Temple was a large room in the Kurosawa House, located in Minakami Village. The room also served as the site where the Cutting Ritual was performed, in order to prepare the Kusabi, an outsider, for the Hidden Ceremony.

This temple also led to the Underground Passage, which then led to the Hellish Abyss.

entries.content:

entries.name: (Term) Spirited Away
entries.content:
The term 'Spirited Aways' or 'Spirited Away' is used to describe a specific group of missing people. These people have completely disappeared without cause or reason, but the most important aspect of their disappearance is that there is suspicion of the paranormal being involved.

When a person has been said to be spirited away, it means that they have been taken by spirits to another place. The bodies of the victims are usually never found. Spirited Aways don't necessarily disappear in similar circumstances or even similar locations.

People can be spirited away (i.e. taken to another place by paranormal influences) and survive (such in the cases of Miku Hinasaki, Mio Amakura and Rei Kurosawa), but they aren't classified as Spirited Aways, because they survived and came back.

entries.name: (Location) Osaka House
entries.content:
The Osaka House was one of the houses of Minakami Village. It is also the first house Mio and Mayu Amakura enter after they are trapped in the village. It is where Mio finds the Camera Obscura, flashlight, and the Spirit Stone Radio as well.

Miyako Sudo is strangled in this house by the ghost of Masumi Makimura, her boyfriend. Before her death, she waited there for him to return so they could escape the village together, but his return brought only her demise and now her spirit haunts the building with him.

entries.name: (Ghost) Broken Neck Woman
entries.content:
Broken Neck Woman, known in Japanese as Kubi ga Oreta Onna (Broken Neck Woman), is a hostile female spirit. She is a woman from the lost All God's Village, now a ghost bearing the twisted, broken neck she suffered upon her death. She is seen walking across the Heaven Bridge following Mayu Amakura, and also at the Tsuchihara grave, later on.

≪ Background ≫
This ghost is presumably a member of the Tsuchihara family, the family which maintained the storehouse/prison. She was on the Heaven Bridge when she saw the Darkness pouring out and starting to engulf the village, so she leapt from the bridge. She seems to have landed on the side of her head as her neck is broken to one side.

Corrupted by the Darkness, she haunts the area close to her death, the Heaven Bridge and the Kiryu house.

≪ Appearance ≫
She appears to have been a young and pretty woman before her death. As a ghost, she has long black hair, a blank stare, and wears a white kimono and obi, with the right side of the kimono overlapping the left.

As a result of her jump from the high bridge, she has a broken neck, causing it to bend at an unnatural angle, and her head permanently rests on her right side.

≪ Battle ≫
This ghost luckily doesn't seem to pull many tricks, other than the usual vanish and reappear trick that all the other ghosts do, but she will crouch slightly. In her Fatal Frame moment, she extends her arms out to the sides and rushes to grab Mio Amakura.

entries.name: (Ghost) Villagers
entries.content:
The Villagers are hostile spirits.

≪ Background ≫
The Villagers are three villagers of Minakami Village who were part of the party who set out to capture Yae and Sae Kurosawa in an attempt to prevent them from escaping the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual. Though Yae managed to escape from their hunt, Sae fell and was captured by them and returned to the village, the villagers also locked Itsuki Tachibana within the Storehouse as a punishment for helping the Kurosawa twins escape.

Desperate due to the awakening of the Hellish Abyss, the villagers decided to sacrifice Sae alone. Sae was hung from the last torii gate by the Veiled Priests and her lifeless body was thrown into the Abyss. With the ritual improperly performed Darkness blasted from the Abyss, engulfing the entire village whilst Sae's vengeful spirit returned along with the Kusabi. The villagers who survived the initial blast were either consumed by the Darkness or killed by Sae and the Kusabi.

With the entire village cursed to relive the night of the Repentance in perpetuity, the villagers continue their search for the fleeing twins.

✦Pole Bearer
Pole Bearer is a hostile male spirit. Not much is known about him when he was alive. He was apart of the search party when the twins Yae and Sae ran away from the village. He is one of the three types of villagers that mostly haunt the streets of All God's Village.

✦Sickle Bearer
Sickle Bearer is a hostile male spirit. Not much of his life is known, however, he was a part of the group to search for Yae and Sae when they escaped the village. He is one of the three types of villagers that mostly haunt the streets of All God's Village.

✦Torch Bearer
Torch Bearer is a hostile male spirit. Not much is known of his life. He was a part of the original group who went to find the twins Yae and Sae after they fled the village. He is one of the three types of villager that mostly haunt the streets of All God's Village.

≪ Battle ≫
They are very basic ghosts, only three types can be encountered. One holds a torch, another carries a sickle, and the last one holds a wooden pole.

entries.name: (Ghost) Masumi Makimura
entries.content:
Masumi Makimura is a hostile male spirit. He was a land surveyor who was surveying the All God's Dam when he disappeared.

≪ Background ≫
About one year ago, Masumi was assigned to survey the area of Minakami for the new dam. However, he unfortunately got trapped in the village during that time. A search was conducted, but ended after 10 days when there was no sign of his whereabouts. During this time, Masumi spent his efforts searching various locations in a desperate attempt to get out. He would leave behind notes as to possible clues of escape routes. Once the search was called off, his girlfriend, Miyako Sudo, retraced his steps to find him and unfortunately getting trapped in the village as well. At some point, the two found each other, but for only a brief moment. Miyako sustained an injury to her leg and was placed in the Osaka House, while Masumi continued his search for a way out, believing the exit was located in the Kurosawa house. Masumi met his unfortunate end at the hands of the Kusabi while he was in the house.

Following his death, Masumi's ghost, filled with regret over not giving Miyako the ring, he ventured back to the Osaka House. But because of the corrupted darkness, when Miyako followed his ghost, he strangled her on sight.

entries.name: (Ghost) Miyako Sudo
entries.content:
Miyako Sudo is a hostile female spirit.

As Mio and Mayu Amakura enter the first house of the Lost Village, they come across journals that describe Miyako's search for her lost boyfriend, Masumi Makimura, who had disappeared in the Minakami Region. Miyako boldly entered the village to search for Masumi, only to have his violent ghost kill her after reuniting. Now she wanders the house she was killed in, forever wondering, "Why?"

≪ Background ≫
Miyako's boyfriend, Masumi, was a surveyor tasked with detailing the Minakami Region for the upcoming construction of the All God's Dam. After getting lost inside All God's Village and being declared missing, Miyako took it upon herself to search for him, only to become trapped in the village herself. After enough searching, the two eventually met up inside the Osaka House; however, Miyako was hurt and had to remain inside the house. In order to search for a way out, Masumi left Miyako to wait inside the Osaka House, promising he would return. Eventually, Masumi was killed in the Kurosawa House by the Kusabi and returned to the Osaka House as a bloodied ghost. Miyako, excited upon his return, followed Masumi's ghost into the Osaka House's back room. Miyako was not reunited with her boyfriend, however, and was instead strangled to death by the angered ghost.

Miyako recorded her experience inside the village in a series of red notebooks. In her entries, she wondered when they could finally leave the village together and wrote about the chilling laughter she heard in the darkness.

≪ Appearance ≫
In life, Miyako was a pretty, 25 year-old woman with long black hair and brown eyes. She wore a short-sleeved white button-up shirt with a pleated navy blue skirt. As a ghost, her appearance drastically changes. Her hair is parted to the side covering one eye, and her clothes are dirty and have ragged edges. There is visible bruising on her neck from the strangulation, and her face takes on a sinister expression.

entries.name: (Location) Twins' Room
entries.content: The Twins' Room is a room in both the Tachibana and Kiryu houses of Minakami Village, which both were used for unspecified rituals connected to the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual. Both rooms present different items. The room in Tachibana House is strung with sacred rope and contains a brazier, two hand-drums, two white kimonos, and offerings presented on a row of shelves similar to an altar, whereas the one in Kiryu House contains two lamps and two mirror stands, along with two dolls, two balls and two red kimonos hanging on racks. Twins are shown kneeling on the cushions on the floor.

entries.name: (Location) Old Tree
entries.content:
The Old Tree is a large tree stump located on the outskirts of Minakami Village, near both the Kureha Shrine and Minakami Cemetery.

It was used to enshrine the bodies of Remaining twins who passed away in the village. Pinwheels and Jizo statues were placed here to comfort their spirits. It also contains the mechanism which, when all four Pinwheel Crests are placed in it, unlocks the path out of the village through the Kureha Shrine. When the passageway is open, the flow of air turns the pinwheels.

entries.name: (Location) Great Hall
entries.content:
The Great Hall is a room in the Kurosawa House.

The corrupted ghosts of Sae Kurosawa and the Kusabi return from the Hellish Abyss, after being sacrificed in two separate rituals, to this very room and massacred the Kurosawa family and other villagers there.

Masumi Makimura came here during his investigation of the Kurosawa House, and was killed in the closet by the Kusabi.

entries.name: (Location) Cell
entries.content: The Cell was one of the rooms of Kurosawa House in Minakami Village. It was used to imprison Outsiders who came to the village and were to be made into Kusabi. It was also used as a room to store books about the village and its rituals. When it was not used as a prison, Sae and Yae Kurosawa would use the cell as a secret place to hold conversations.

entries.name: (Location) Minakami Cemetery
entries.content:
Minakami Cemetery is the cemetery of Minakami Village, which is both the resting place of the village’s deceased and where the villagers go to honor their ancestors.

There are two paths which connect this cemetery to the villages itself, one coming from Misono Hill and the other that can be found at the Old Tree.

entries.name: (Ghost) Akane and Azami Kiryu
entries.content:
Akane Kiryu (桐生 茜, Kiryū Akane) and Azami Kiryu (桐生 薊, Kiryū Azami) are hostile female spirits. They were twin sisters residing in All God's Village and previous victims of the Crimson Sacrifice Ritual. As Twin Shrine Maidens, their duty was to perform the ritual and ensure the village's survival. Although they succeeded in this, their love for one another ran deep and Akane, the surviving twin, suffered from serious trauma. Both of their spirits remained following the Repentance, trapped within the lost village.

≪ Background ≫
Although Azami left the womb first, and therefore was born first, by village custom she was the younger sister. As the elder sister, Akane was given the task of sacrificing Azami once the time of the ritual came. During this time the village was in a desperate condition, and so their ritual was held while the two were still quite young. Nonetheless, both sisters were resolute in performing the sacrifice. During the ceremony, Akane had difficulty with the task at hand and a Veiled Priest attempted to help her. Azami refused this, and insisted that her sister should be the only one who takes her life. Upon completion of the ritual, the Hellish Abyss was appeased and Akane became a Remaining.

The sacrifice did not pass without taking its toll on Akane's psyche. Feeling tremendous guilt over the loss of her sister, Akane began to fall into depression. Hoping to ease the burden of the psychological trauma, her father, Yoshitatsu Kiryu, a dollmaker, built for her a special doll in the image of Azami. Akane became so attached to the doll, whispering to it as if it were indeed her sister, that a spirit possessed it and began to control her. Yoshitatsu was able to see the darkness taking hold of the doll and his daughter, and, in a dream, he was asked by Azami's spirit to hang the doll and throw it into the Hellish Abyss to destroy it and free her sister. However, the doll told Akane of his plan and so Akane dismantled the doll and hid the pieces. Yoshitatsu was not able to save his daughter and he was soon strangled by Akane, now fully controlled by the evil spirit. The spirit then consumed Akane's soul and the Kiryu family was ended.

During Mio Amakura's search through the Kiryu house, she encounters the hostile ghosts of Akane and the possessed doll. Azami's spirit reaches out to Mio as well, directing her to the hidden doll parts and instructing her to "Kill me". By this, she means for Mio to destroy the evil doll and finally set Akane's soul free. With the doll's head, left arm, right arm and eyes, Mio was able to open the Earth bridge tunnel beneath the house and continue on her way to releasing the village from darkness.

≪ Appearance ≫
Akane, Azami, and the doll of Azami, all look identical to one another by their height they appear to be between the ages of 7 and 11. They wear gray furisode-style kimonos with a small fan design in the lower end and a light-gray obi, and wear white tabi socks. They have long hair that they let fall and cover their eyes, reminiscent of traditional, female Japanese ghosts.

≪ Battle ≫
Akane's and the doll's ghosts will always attack together. Therefore, it is key not to get caught between the two of them (unfortunately, this is the exact situation in which they are first encountered). More importantly, only the ghost of Akane can receive damage while both ghosts are able to deal damage. Pictures taken of the doll will push it back, but it is otherwise unharmed. A definite pattern can be observed wherein one ghost attacks, prompting a shot from the camera, while the other ghost flanks Mio from behind. Thus, it is important to be aware of both ghosts, rather than focusing on just one at a time, and shots of both ghosts at once are ideal.

There are multiple ways to distinguish between the two ghosts:

‣ One method entails listening closely as a ghost approaches. Akane will sound like any other ghost, her footsteps creaking on old wood. The doll however sounds like clattering blocks of wood impacting upon each other, emulating the sound of a wooden puppet quite well.
‣ The other method entails waiting until a ghost begins to attack. Once close enough either ghost will raise her arms. If the ghost is the doll, its head will quickly drop and the camera will no longer be effective. If it is Akane, she will raise her head and show her face. This method not only distinguishes which ghost is vulnerable, but also allows for Akane's Fatal Frame chance.
‣ Another way to tell the difference between the two is by looking carefully at their face when they reach for (or attack) Mio. The real one, which is Akane, can see a bit more of her face while the possessed doll does not show much of her face at all.
‣ This method is possibly the safest and entails listening for the ghosts' voices. Upon appearing Azami's ghost will whisper "Why do you kill?" in a girlish voice. The doll's ghost utters the same words, albeit in a noticeably deeper and more grim voice.
‣ The doll does not have a mouth; but Akane does.

entries.name: (Ghost) Man in Dark
entries.content:
Man in Dark is a hostile male spirit.

Man in Dark was a resident of the Minakami Village, though which family he belonged to or his profession are unknown. The only thing truly known about him was that he was killed by the Malice during The Repentance, during which his soul was torn from him and he was condemned to be trapped in the Darkness for an eternity, though he does not feel any pain.

entries.name: (Ghost) Falling Woman
entries.content:
Falling Woman is a hostile female spirit.

≪ Background ≫
Not much is known about her other than the spirit stone she leaves behind. After the failed ritual, she sensed the darkness coming and instead being trapped in the dark, she decides to jump to her death. However, due to the nature of the darkness and the repeating of that horrific night, she continues to jump in agony, still suffering within the dark.

≪ Battle ≫
This is actually a pretty tricky ghost to fight, as when every time she vanishes she will attempt to fall next to Mio. If she happen to be close enough to her when she hits the ground, Mio is either going to be startled with fear or thrown off balance, and the Falling Woman will grab Mio while she is in this current state. However, this is also when the Fatal Frame shot can be done. This is probably one of the hardest Fatal Frame shots to take, as she's only vulnerable to the Fatal Frame when she's falling in mid-air. Also, the fact that she will mostly fall right next to Mio makes this attempt a big gamble, since missing the shot will leave her vulnerable to the ghost stunning her and allowing them to grab Mio.

However, she is slow when moving around since she's broken both legs (and possibly arms) in her fall, only able to crawl by pushing her knees and elbows against the floor. The only real threat she presents is if she catches Mio by surprise. If Mio can see her coming, it's easy to take good shots.

entries.name: (Ghost) Woman in Box
entries.content:
Woman in Box, known in Japanese as "Hako ni Kakureta Onna" (Woman hidden in box), is a hostile female spirit. She is one of the violent spirits that haunt the lost All God's Village and was yet another witness of the Repentance, choosing to hide in a kimono box with her newborn child to escape the coming darkness. She became trapped, however, and she and her child were both swallowed by the darkness.

≪ Background ≫
Woman in Box's true name is never revealed. However, it can be assumed that she belonged to the Osaka family, as she hid inside a kimono box within the Osaka House. The identity of her child is also unknown, and it never physically appears. Not much is known of her true identity, aside from her death from the darkness of the Repentance.

≪ Appearance ≫
Woman in Box always appears by crawling out of a box or well. She moves in a lethargic manner, taking slow steps forward and stopping when close enough to attack. She stays bent forward with her long hair covering her face most times, and after stopping and raising her head, her face can be seen as aged. She also wears a plain kimono, common to other inhabitants of the village.

≪ Battle ≫
Woman in box has a very distinct pattern of attack from other ghosts. While slowly lurching forward, the camera's Capture Circle frequently senses and loses shutter chances for short periods of time. After she has gotten close enough to Mio, she raises her head and arms and quickly moves forward in a grabbing motion, during which the camera senses a Fatal Frame. Once enough damage has been dealt to her (leaving her with about 1/3 of her health), she begins to disappear and move around the room more frequently. She also forgoes the slow lurching, and begins to charge quickly at Mio with her arms outstretched.

Battling her can be nerve-wracking at first, however, her attack patterns eventually become easy to exploit. One strategy is to "bait" her Fatal Frame by getting close and quickly backing away, prompting her to raise her head and attack. Another, more cautious strategy is to exploit the shutter chances during her forward movement. Unlike the Fatal Frames, the shutter chances occur more frequently, and she does not disappear immediately afterward. When she begins charging, it is best to stay in an open area, as she will run from behind walls. During her charge, however, there is a much longer chance to shoot a fatal frame, pushing her back and dealing a lot of damage.

entries.name: (Ghost) Woman in Dark
entries.content: Woman in Dark is a hostile female spirit. Not much is known of her life prior to the ritual, but it can be assumed she was an inhabitant of All God's Village. She was killed at some point during the Repentance and begs for help from anyone she sees.

entries.name: (Ghost) Yoshitatsu Kiryu
entries.content:
Yoshitatsu Kiryu is a hostile male spirit. He is the father of Akane and Azami Kiryu.

≪ Biography ≫
After his daughters performed the ritual, Akane (The Remaining) fell into a deep depression. Her eyes were filled with pain and guilt, and her heart became consumed with sorrow. Her father, Yoshitasu Kiryu felt sympathetic towards her. In order to ease his daughter's pain, he made a doll much like her deceased twin. His pure intentions to bring a smile to his sad daughter's face only brought about the demise of the family and ultimately the end of his bloodline.

Akane grew very attached to the doll her father made her, so attached that she began whispering in her ears and taking her wherever she went. Soon, the doll became possessed by a malicious spirit that controlled its movements as if life has been brought to the doll.

In a dream, Azami told her father that the doll is possessed and instructed him to throw it into the Hellish Abyss to free her sister from the doll's influence.

The doll informed Akane of her father's plan to destroy the doll, so Akane removed her arms and head and hid them away.

Yoshitatsu is determined to end the doll's life in order to save his only daughter. However, he is hesitant because the doll resembles his deceased daughter. He said that he would destroy the doll, even if she looks like his daughter, even if it meant killing her twice. He knew there was a chance that he could go blind by looking into the Hellish Abyss, but he was willing to sacrifice his sight to save Akane.

Unfortunately, he fails to fulfill his duty and is strangled to death by the possessed Akane.
